visual_appeal: Reduce the hero portrait from approximately 110 px to 96 px and move the text block 12 px left. Keep the character name dominant, but give the metadata and banked amount more breathing room.

Reduce the density of the progress-bar segmentation: use divisions every 10% rather than the current tightly spaced ticks. The repeated vertical strokes make the roster look busier than its information warrants.
Use a consistent 12 px internal inset across the hero, current-character strip, roster and footer; the present mixture of inset depths makes the composition feel assembled rather than art-directed.
state_colours: Keep all four state hues, but make the chip treatment genuinely consistent. RESTING still reads as a brown button while FULL reads as a dark status label. Use a common near-black base with a 20–25% state tint, a 1 px state border and matching text brightness.
Add a small bed/rest symbol to RESTING chips, matching the check, star and warning symbols in the other states. Colour should reinforce a complete icon-and-label vocabulary.

In the compact tooltip, show the not-resting character's banked percentage as well as the red warning. Use a two-part line such as 20% banked · Not filling rather than replacing the amount with Outside.
character_identity: On the saved-look card, increase the face source resolution where available rather than enlarging a visibly soft crop to approximately 145 px. Preserve the required face-plus-class-badge treatment.

Use one character-name size hierarchy across windows: approximately 28 px for the hero, 22 px for the detail card and 14 px for roster names. The detail card currently gives the speech bubble and portrait more authority than the character's name.

In the exhausted-rest toast, label the two identities explicitly: Le Jette: rested XP depleted, followed by Next: Le Dette. Keep the next character's portrait beside the second line so it cannot be mistaken for the character named in the heading.
default_theme: Darken and desaturate the alternating roster fills to approximately #211C16 and #282118. The current brown bands compete with orange progress bars and flatten the state hierarchy.
Reduce the default portrait's gold outer rim to 1–2 px while retaining the required state-coloured ring. The heavy double rim gives the portrait more decorative weight than the rest of the window.
Lower the contrast of the hero's scenic background by approximately 20%, with a dark overlay behind metadata. It should provide atmosphere without introducing another competing texture.
elvui_wc3_fit: The warm recessed wells are a better match, but the large dark, vertically streaked header still feels visually empty beside the reference Character window. Reduce the title/header region by 12–16 px and preserve the inherited outer skin.

Use the host's actual font face, outline and size for addon-owned buttons and small utility labels. The renders mix a softer serif information treatment with tightly outlined host controls; reserve the decorative face for titles and character names.

Apply the same inherited inner-well treatment to the alert bodies and character card. The current alerts expose much stronger wood texture than the main roster, so related surfaces still appear to belong to different widget families.
alerts_ux: Increase alert body copy to at least 13 px at native scale, with 4 px between lines and 12 px left/right padding. The logout banner's character-location line is substantially less readable than its headline.
Give every dismiss button a minimum 24 × 24 px hit target, even if the visible red cross stays 14–16 px. Leave at least 8 px between the gear and close targets.

In move mode, make each placeholder's entire body visibly draggable with a subtle dashed inner outline, and change the footer to Drag anywhere on this panel. Preserve the individual Reset buttons and the Esc-menu attachment explanation.

Keep the logout instruction noninteractive, but shorten the headline to Rest at an inn before logging out and put Cancel logout, then hearth to Feathermoon Stronghold beneath it. This separates the goal from the manual steps without implying a protected action button.
readability: Raise roster metadata, footer information and options explanatory copy to a minimum of 13 px at native scale. Increase roster rows from roughly 58 px to 62 px if necessary rather than compressing the second line.

Reserve a fixed-width location column or move last-seen time into a tooltip. Thunderbrew... is truncated even in this small fixture roster; the player should not have to decode a clipped inn name beside class and level.
Replace Full since 1d 16h ago with Full for 1d 16h. Replace More rest is wasted. with Rested XP capped — play this character. Both changes improve fluency and make the consequence concrete.
Use at least #C8BFAF for secondary text on dark wells, and avoid strong outlines on small body copy. Keep the names in their settled class colours.
layout_polish: Rework the timeline tooltip placement. In the supplied scene it covers another character's lane and progress information. Prefer a fixed detail area below the chart, or place the tooltip outside the plot with screen-edge clamping.
Anchor Then Le Bankken, full in 19h 11m directly beneath step 2, not beneath step 1. Its current alignment makes the sequence read as an explanatory footnote rather than the third action in the plan.
Give ROSTER and TIMELINE minimum 64 × 24 px targets and an 8 px gap. Their tiny labels currently compete with the summary line instead of behaving like clear view controls.

Rebalance the character card: move the name and metadata upward by approximately 16 px and reduce the empty gap below the speech bubble. Align the status chip and progress summary to the same 12 px content inset.

Separate the footer's account controls from display controls with a 16 px gap or a subtle divider. Unlink, paired-account status, account filtering and hidden-character visibility currently read as one crowded control strip.
delight: Make speech respond to state and location rather than merely decorating the portrait: a capped character can invite play, a resting character can mention the inn, and a non-resting character can ask to be brought indoors. Keep it to one short line in the hero.
Give the 48-hour timeline a clear completion moment: a small state-coloured endpoint diamond plus the exact completion time on hover or focus. Do not rely solely on a glowing circular endpoint.

Use a brief, restrained 250–350 ms emphasis when a new character becomes PLAY NEXT, with no continuous shimmer and no animation when reduced motion is enabled. This would make the recommendation feel responsive without turning the roster into a dashboard of effects.

overall_notes: A meaningful improvement over the real baseline: the recommendation is unmistakable, the numbered recovery plan is useful, the current character no longer has a misleading empty track, and the timeline correctly distinguishes stopped accumulation. The warm wells also recover much of the WC3 relationship. This is a strong functional addon, but not yet demanding-user approval at 9+: small typography, clipped metadata, tooltip occlusion, inconsistent surface treatment and crowded secondary controls remain visible production-quality issues. Preserve the core hierarchy and settled portrait rules; spend the next pass on native-scale legibility and alignment rather than adding decoration. The simulator's inability to render a live model is not a defect and was not scored as one.
